prompt: A central bank unexpectedly raises its policy rate by 50 basis points. All else equal, the most likely immediate effect on the domestic currency and bond prices is:
explanation: A rate hike makes domestic assets more attractive to foreign investors, increasing demand for the domestic currency — it appreciates. Higher interest rates mean higher discount rates for bond cash flows, so bond prices fall (price and yield move inversely). Options B and C each get one of the two directions wrong. This is a classic tested pairing: rate increases → currency strengthens AND bond prices fall.
